channel.description: Latest articles from The GW Hatchet (gwhatchet.com)

item.title: Perspective: GW must combat the homogenization of Latin America
item.description: Many think that Latin American culture is only Mexican or Caribbean, or that accents between regions do not diverge. We, the GW community, must actively work to push against these stereotypes: by asking people about their cultures, being open and empathetic. Latin American culture is deeply ingrained in the United States, although not always acknowledged by citizens in its entirety.

item.title: Women’s basketball falls 67-52 to George Mason in sixth consecutive rivalry defeat
item.description: Hopes were high following an overtime victory over Richmond, a top contender in the Atlantic 10, but the magic was unable to be replicated as George Mason took a commanding lead starting in the second quarter.

item.title: Column: Classes aren’t connecting Trump to authoritarian trends
item.description: It is the responsibility of a higher-education institution to expose students to information they may not get anywhere else and encourage them to make connections they may not otherwise make so that they can understand the true ramifications of national developments.

item.title: Crime log: Student reports person following her into Dakota
item.description: Unlawful Entry The Dakota 2/11/2026 – 12:40 p.m. Open Case The GW Police Department responded to a report of a female non-GW-affiliated person following a student into the building. A staff member escorted the non-GW-affiliated person off GW property. A GWPD canvas of the area for the person failed to locate them. – Case open....

item.title: Anonymous trustee, GW donations to fund humanitarian internships supporting Gaza
item.description: A $200,000 donation from an anonymous trustee will fund 14 paid internships supporting World Central Kitchen’s Gaza relief operations in D.C. and Jordan this summer.

item.title: Meet the candidates vying to lead GW Law’s student government
item.description: Candidates for SBA president and executive vice president said they hope to boost transparency between law school officials and students surrounding broader University challenges, like federal investigations and budget constraints.

item.title: Officials slash journal subscriptions as part of FY2026 budget cuts
item.description: GW Libraries & Academic Innovation slashed academic journal subscriptions at Gelman Library by 6 percent and at Himmelfarb Health Sciences Library by 10 percent as part of fiscal year 2026 budget cuts, officials confirmed Friday.

item.title: Students, alum condemn GW’s handling of campus antisemitism in U.S. Commission testimony
item.description: Two current students and an alum testified that persistent antisemitism from fellow students, anti-Israel comments from faculty members and a lack of University response have made them feel unsafe on campus.

item.title: JEC sets SGA election dates for April 16, 17
item.description: Students can vote for SGA president, vice president and senators from 9 a.m. on April 16 until 9 p.m. on April 17, the latest dates the body has held its elections since its inception in 1976.

item.title: Castro’s return sparks record-breaking 104-77 win over La Salle
item.description: Men's basketball set a program record for most points in an A-10 regulation game in a 104-77 win against La Salle on Tuesday night.
